ClaudeTitleOutro was deliberately NOT used for the outro because its '@NikBearBrown' handle is hardcoded in the component source (runtime/remotion/src/scenes/ClaudeTitleOutro.tsx:19) with no prop override — using it here would have misattributed this personal project. metadata.note: Real progress recap of C:\Users\kavya\OneDrive\Desktop\CabStream, grounded in that repo's actual git log (not illustrative/fabricated). CabStream is a real, independently verifiable data-engineering project: Kafka -> Spark/Delta medallion lakehouse on Azure Databricks -> dbt Gold star schema -> Claude-powered Text-to-SQL agent, eventually processing 1.57B NYC taxi/rideshare trips (per the project's own README). This reel covers WEEK 1 ONLY (commits 2026-06-09 through 2026-06-15, confirmed via `git log --all --format='%ad %h %s' --date=short`): Kafka docker setup + producer (taxi-trips topic) on 06-09, Kafka-to-Delta bronze ingestion with verification on 06-11, silver parse/validate/deduplicate job on 06-12, weather-join silver job + dbt Gold layer on 06-15. The large verified metrics (1.57B rows, 99.9% pass rate, 86.9% rideshare dominance, COVID story, the Text-to-SQL agent) all land in LATER commits (ac80e80 'Phase 2 verified metrics' onward, into July/August per the full git log) and are explicitly called out on screen as NOT part of week 1 — this reel does not backdate them. GitHub username on the repo's merged PRs is literally 'Kavya-Mehta', confirming this is the user's own project.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Kavya, and this video is about my first week building CabStream, a real-time data pipeline project. This narration is AI-generated with Kokoro text-to-speech, reading a script I wrote and reviewed. Day one of CabStream was an empty repo. Day six had a Kafka producer, a Delta bronze layer, a deduplicated silver layer with weather joined in, and a dbt gold layer. Here's what actually got built, in order.

beats.narration_text: Here's the idea: week one wasn't wiring up a demo pipeline. It's the full medallion architecture, scaffolded end to end — bronze, silver, and gold, in six days.

beats.narration_text: Four stages, one week. A Kafka producer reading NYC taxi parquet and publishing to the taxi-trips topic, day one. Bronze — streamed into Delta Lake, with ingestion verification. Silver — parsed, validated, deduplicated, then joined against weather data. And gold — the dbt layer, scaffolded the same week. Bronze, silver, and gold, all standing by day six.

beats.narration_text: What week one didn't have yet: no scale numbers. The one-point-five-seven-billion rows, the ninety-nine-point-nine percent pass rate, the COVID story — all of that came later, in a phase that gets its own commit calling out the verified metrics. Week one built the shape of the pipeline. It hadn't run it at scale yet.
